item.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
item.description: Global fashion retailers, including Zara and H&M, diverted orders worth $254 million from Bangladesh amid labour unrest and rising costs, with India emerging as the biggest beneficiary ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global fashion retailers, including Zara and H&M, shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said. Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest. Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing. The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40 per cent of its manufacturing jobs. Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia also benefit India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said. Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades. The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all workers would resume work from Saturday. Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards. Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers’ representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh. He said retailers already factor political instability and labour unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves “hard to justify” and raising “serious doubts” about whether the unrest was more than an excuse. Factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business. Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment. Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11 per cent and Trident gaining about 5 per cent. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living, KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles, rose around 2 per cent each. M Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers “at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying”. More business at risk Factory owners said the bigger concern was that diversions of business could become permanent. Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources. But Chowdhury said that price became secondary when brands were under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines. India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said. Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added. The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments. Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business. “Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest,” Alam said. “They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions.” Political tensions surrounding former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption. Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved. “The challenge is restoring buyers’ confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions,” he said. “Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists.”

item.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
item.description: The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry

Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry The airport operator has sought government permission to invest in airlines, citing the need for a tenfold increase in daily flights in a market dominated by IndiGo and Air India

| Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 9:18 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday. Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000. "And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here.

In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had ruled out entering the airlines business, saying that it is never a good strategy to compete with customers. Adani group runs eight airports in the country, including the ones in the financial capital and the satellite city of Navi Mumbai, and also Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati, which ferry over one-fourth of the country's air passenger traffic. The airline business has been reduced to a virtual duopoly with two strong domestic carriers -- the Tata Group-led Air India and Rahul Bhatia-run IndiGo, ruling the skies with a 90 per cent market share.

Problems at IndiGo last year, which led to thousands of flight cancellations, led to voices demanding more airlines to operate in the country.

Home / Markets / News / Sebi aims to cut FPI onboarding time to five business days: Chairman

Sebi aims to cut FPI onboarding time to five business days: Chairman Pandey said the regulator has also proposed removing the additional disclosure framework for FPIs, bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards

Over the past few months, Sebi has taken several measures to ease the compliance burden for FPIs | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 3:55 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Markets regulator Sebi is aiming to reduce the onboarding time for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from several months to as little as five business days through digital workflows and system integration, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday. Addressing the 17th Capital Markets Conference organised by ASSOCHAM, Pandey said the regulator has also proposed removing the additional disclosure framework for FPIs, bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards. "Through digital workflows and system integration, we aim to cut FPI onboarding from months to as little as five business days," Pandey said. Over the past few months, Sebi has taken several measures to ease the compliance burden for FPIs.

Under the SWAGAT-FI (Single Window Automatic and Generalised Access for Trusted Foreign Investors) initiative, around 740 FPIs, accounting for nearly 17 per cent of FPI assets under custody, have registered. Also Read

Sebi studying Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal, minority interests key: Pandey

Sebi takes minority shareholders' rights seriously: Chairman Tuhin Pandey

Sebi may scrutinise Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal over RPT, shareholder worry premium

FPI buying lifts markets, but India's external outlook remains uncertain premium

Sebi appoints auditor to probe Coffee Day Enterprises' fund diversion

"SWAGAT-FI gives trusted, low-risk FPIs single-window access, simpler compliance and longer KYC review cycles," he added. On the regulatory front, Pandey said Sebi is undertaking a comprehensive review of the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) framework to eliminate duplicative disclosures in filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). The regulator also plans to replace multiple stock exchange fines for the same compliance lapse with a single penalty. Sebi is simultaneously reviewing the Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) framework, which governs initial public offerings (IPOs), follow-on public offerings (FPOs), preferential issues and qualified institutional placements (QIPs). The review will also cover the SME IPO framework and the Innovators Growth Platform.

For stock brokers, the regulator is exploring a graded compliance framework under which regulatory obligations would be aligned with a broker's scale, client exposure and dependence on technology. Pandey said the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is also working towards harmonising the regulatory frameworks governing Investment Advisers and Mutual Fund Distributors. On the technology front, the regulator is exploring the development of a domestically governed artificial intelligence (AI) model for the securities market, enabling smaller regulated entities to access secure and affordable AI solutions. Guidelines on the responsible use of AI are being prepared, while a proposed AI sandbox will allow innovators to test applications in a controlled environment, he said.

In the corporate bond market, Sebi is developing a market-making framework in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Ministry of Finance, focusing on liquidity, market infrastructure and access to repo facilities. Fixed Income Channel Partners will help expand bond distribution via regulated online platforms, while Phase II of Demat 2.0 will enable secondary-market trading in tokenised bonds. In the cash market, the regulator is reviewing the framework for short selling and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) to improve liquidity and price discovery. For Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), the regulator is simplifying requirements linked to investor consent, related-party transactions, co-investments and exits.

In the case of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), Sebi aims to reduce the listing timeline from six working days to three days and simplify the process for rights issues. Highlighting the growth of India's capital markets, Pandey said companies raised around Rs 9 lakh crore through equity and debt in the first seven months of the current financial year. So far, 235 IPOs have collectively raised approximately Rs 1.45 lakh crore, while more than Rs 5 lakh crore has been mobilised through corporate bonds.

Home / Industry / News / Centre urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts

Centre urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts States need to identify their power requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Union Minister Shripad Naik said

Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power generation, which has wasted clean energy

Reuters Nov 27 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 12:31 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity that has no buyers. States need to identify their power requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi. The lack of battery energy storage resulted in states scrambling for power to meet their evening and night demand as the El Nino weather pattern pushed up consumption this year. The unexpected surge in demand strained India's power system in September and October despite the country having surplus solar energy, Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said at the conference.   Peak power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than a year earlier, Agarwal said. "There were days we could barely meet their evening peak demand despite having surplus clean energy during the day," Agarwal said. Naik also urged states to speed up payments tied to the acquisition of land for transmission projects, saying slow payments have led to huge delays. Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power generation, which has wasted clean energy.
